_meta.indication: Treatment of adult and pediatric patients 12 years of age or older with unresectable or metastatic melanoma.

pivotal_trials.design: Randomized (1:1), double-blinded, active-controlled trial comparing OPDUALAG (nivolumab 480 mg and relatlimab 160 mg IV every 4 weeks) versus nivolumab 480 mg IV every 4 weeks.
pivotal_trials.population: Adult patients with previously untreated metastatic or unresectable Stage III or IV melanoma.
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Progression-free survival (PFS) determined by Blinded Independent Central Review (BICR) using RECIST v1.1.
pivotal_trials.result: Median PFS 10.1 months (95% CI 6.4, 15.7) with OPDUALAG vs 4.6 months (95% CI 3.4, 5.6) with nivolumab; HR 0.75 (95% CI 0.62, 0.92); p=0.0055. ORR 43% vs 33%. Final OS not statistically significant (HR 0.80, 95% CI 0.64, 1.01).

key_safety: Most common adverse reactions (≥20%) are musculoskeletal pain, fatigue, rash, pruritus, and diarrhea. Most common laboratory abnormalities (≥20%) are decreased hemoglobin, decreased lymphocytes, increased AST, increased ALT, and decreased sodium. Serious risks include severe and fatal immune-mediated adverse reactions.
target_moa: Fixed-dose combination of nivolumab (a PD-1 blocking antibody) and relatlimab (a LAG-3 blocking antibody); relatlimab blocks LAG-3 and reduces LAG-3 pathway-mediated inhibition of the immune response, and nivolumab blocks PD-1, together increasing T-cell activation compared with either antibody alone.
modality: mAb (fixed-dose combination of two IgG4 monoclonal antibodies)

advisory_committee.vote: The application was not referred to an FDA advisory committee.

summary.text: Opdualag received traditional (regular) approval based on a statistically significant PFS improvement in the Phase 3 RELATIVITY-047 trial. The application had Fast Track designation and was reviewed under Priority review; it was not referred to an advisory committee and was approved on the first cycle.
